key_insight: GTFS4EV uses open transit data to plan electric bus electrification and solar PV integration, showing that opportunity charging can sharply cut battery size, peak load, and charging costs for Dakar’s BRT.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps transit planners co-design charging strategy, battery sizing, and PV capacity under real operational constraints in data-scarce cities.
method: Simulate bus operations from GTFS schedules and routes
Compare electrification strategies: depot only, terminal and depot, terminal only
Evaluate battery sizing, charging load, costs, emissions, and PV integration
evidence_signal: In the Dakar BRT case study, the 'Terminal and depot' strategy reduced minimum battery capacity from 285 to 57 kWh per bus and peak charging load from 5.3 to 1.5 MW versus depot-only charging.
watch_item: Results depend on the accuracy and completeness of GTFS data and may need local validation of traffic, charging behavior, and grid/PV assumptions.
paper_title: Planning electric bus systems with solar photovoltaic integration using open transit data: A case study of the Dakar BRT
